items.title: View downloads of Working Papers
items.text:
Downloads aren't only the way to view Working Papers

This metric is only tracking the links that people click to download the Working Papers. If someone views the Working Paper's PDF embed on the page without clicking the download link, that won't be counted in this metric. If you want to track how many people are viewing the Working Papers pages, visit How to see page views.

items.title: Visit CERG's Google Analytics page
items.text:
Ensure you are logged in to your SFU Google account and have gotten access by IT Services. If you don't have access, request analytics access here.

Go to Google Analytics Engagement page

If you aren't already on the "Engagement" page, click the "Engagement" tab in the left sidebar.

Google Analytics Engagement page

Link Clicks vs Actions

On the Engagement page, you'll see two charts: Link Clicks and Actions. We will focus on Link Clicks chart, as that gives us a more reliable view of engagement.

items.title: Choose a date range
items.text:
Click the date range in the top right corner of the page to select a date range for which you want to see page views. You can select a custom date range or choose from the preset options.

Google Analytics date range selection

Tracking Views Over Time

When tracking page views over time, it's important to keep the same date range consistent for accurate comparisons. I'd recommend tracking by month as it is simple to visualize and provides a good balance between capturing enough data and avoiding short-term fluctuations.

items.title: Find metrics for a specific working paper
items.text:
If you want to know how many people clicked the download link for a specific Working Paper, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the Working Paper link in the chart. If it was recently published and has lots of traction, it should be on the first page. Otherwise, you can use the arrows at the bottom of the chart to navigate through the pages until you find the link.

The link name should look like this: Read Working Paper #21

Google Analytics Working Paper link highlighted

items.title: Find metrics for a specific button
items.text:
If you want to know how many people clicked a specific button on the CERG website, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the button text manually in the chart.

The link text should match the button text on the CERG website. For example, if you want to see how many people clicked the "Learn more about Andy" button, look for that text in the chart.

Google Analytics number of button clicks

items.title: Find metrics for a specific URL
items.text:
If you want to know how many people and where they came from to get to a specific page or URL on the CERG website, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the button text manually in the chart:

  1. Right click on the chart and select "Drill Down".
  2. Find the URL that you want to track. This will give you a general sense of clicked on a button to get to that URL.
  3. Left click on it to make it bold, then right click on it and select "Drill Down". This will show which pages people came from to get to that URL.
  4. To reset, click the reset icon in the top left corner of the chart.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Example of finding metrics for a working paper URL

Link Source: {not set}

When drilling down to find metrics for a specific URL, you may see some links with the source listed as {not set}. This means that the link was clicked from an external source, such as a social media post or an email.

If you want to track a specific source of traffic, visit Analyze page views.

items.title: Find metrics from a specific source
items.text:
If you want to know how many people visited a page using a link from a specific source, you can use the search bar to filter the results by source.

Enter in the search bar: ?utm_source=example where example is the source you want to track.

For example, if you want to see how many people visited a page from ChatGPT, you would enter: ?utm_source=chatgpt

items.title: How to set up link tracking
items.text:
This guide will walk you through the process of setting up link tracking for external content CERG produces.

Link tracking is important for understanding how many people are clicking on links to CERG content from external sources, such as social media posts or emails. By setting up link tracking, you can gain insights into the effectiveness of your outreach efforts and make data-driven decisions to improve engagement.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Sources
items.text: Each link you want to track should have a source associated with it. The source you use will be dependent on what platform or channel the link is being shared from.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: List of sources you can use
items.text:
• email - for links shared in emails (e.g. CERG newsletter)
  • linkedin - for links shared on LinkedIn
  • sfu - for links shared to SFU (e.g. SFU News, SFU social media posts)
  • facebook - for links shared on Facebook

etc.

Using a consistent source name is important for accurate tracking.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Attach the source to the link
items.text:
To attach the source to a link, append ?utm_source=example to the end of the link, where example is the source you want to track.

So sharing a link to a CERG event on LinkedIn would look like this:

https://www.sfu.ca/politics/CERG/events/fall-2026-wp-21-alternatives-to-fossil-fuels.html?utm_source=linkedin
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Track the link in Google Analytics
items.text: Once you have set up link tracking, you can track the link in Google Analytics by following the steps in Analyze page views.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Archive a team member
items.text:
When a team member leaves CERG, do not delete their page.

Instead, we can archive their team member page. This removes it from the CERG Team page while keeping it accessible through links from other pages (e.g. working papers, events), essentially unlisting their profile rather than deleting it.

  1. In AEM, navigate to the team member's page under CERG team:

    CERG Team in AEM

  2. Right click on the team member's page and select Page Properties.

  3. In the Basic tab, add the tag unlisted to the Tags field.
  4. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.

items.title: Updating the agrivoltaics page
items.text:
This guide will walk you through the process of updating the agrivoltaics page on the CERG website. Most of this is also a duplicate from updating the homepage.

You can edit the Agrivoltaics page through this link below.

Prerequisite

You must be signed into your SFU account and have access to AEM in order to make changes. If you do not have access, please contact Andy to request access.

Go to Agrivoltaics page on AEM

items.title: Change the banner image
items.text:
Prerequisite

You have already uploaded the image to AEM that you want added to the banner. If you haven't done this yet, please follow the steps in Uploading new photos and documents.

  1. Double click on the banner image or right click and select Edit.
  2. Select the Image tab.
  3. Drag and drop a new image into the Image field from the sidebar.
  4. Press the Crop button to crop the image to a 3:1 (Banner) aspect ratio.
  5. If you'd like to include a caption, select the Advanced Image Properties tab and enter your text in the Description text field.
  6. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Changing the banner image on the Agrivoltaics page

items.title: Update text content
items.text:
1. Right click on the text you want to edit and select Edit.
  2. Make your changes in the text editor that appears.
  3. Use the formatting buttons a the top of the editor to format your text, add links, or add images.
  4. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.

Text with {{ }}

Don't edit text inside {{ }} — it's a variable placeholder auto-filled by the site, and editing it breaks the component.

If that text needs to change (e.g., event, working paper, or news article info), update it via the documentation for that content type instead; changes will automatically reflect on the Agrivoltaics page.

items.title: Change photos in the photo gallery
items.text:
Each photo gallery on our website is its own folder in AEM's DAM (Digital Asset Manager). To change the photos in the gallery, you will need to upload new photos to the folder and delete old ones.

Go to the Agrivoltaics image gallery folder in DAM

Images already in DAM somewhereImages not yet uploaded to DAM
  1. Go into DAM and find the image(s) you want to add to the gallery.
  2. Select the image(s), right click, and select the Copy button
  3. Navigate to the Agrivoltaics image gallery folder and select Paste to add the image(s) to the gallery.
  4. Reorder, delete, or edit the images in the gallery as needed.
  5. Make sure you activate the image(s) to save your changes.
  1. Follow the instructions for uploading new images to DAM first.
  2. Add a caption to the images if you want to (see instructions below).
  3. Copy the images to the Agrivoltaics image gallery folder using the instructions in the first tab.
  4. Make sure you activate the image(s) to save your changes.

items.title: Adding captions
items.text:
If you want to add captions to the images in the gallery, you can do so by editing the image properties in DAM.

  1. Right click on the image and select Open.
  2. Enter your text in the Description text field.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Changing the photo gallery's images on the Agrivoltaics page

items.title: Add/remove a sponsor
items.text:
Prerequisite

In order to ensure proper sizing for all logos, please run your image through this image resizer before uploading it to DAM.

Then you can proceed with uploading the logo to DAM under the Logos folder .

  1. Ensure you have properly resized the logo and uploaded it to DAM under the Logos folder.
  2. Duplicate an existing sponsor card by right clicking on it and selecting Copy.

  6. Go to the Advanced tab and change the Link to field to the sponsor's website.
  7. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.

Place sponsor cards in the first two columns

items.text:
Prerequisite

Ensure the image(s) you want added to the banner have already been uploaded to AEM. If not, follow the steps in Uploading new photos and documents.

Due to AEM's limitations, the banner is a carousel of images on desktop, and one static image on mobile. Each has its own way of changing the images.

items.title: Change the desktop carousel images
items.text:
Each banner image on the website is its own unlisted page on the site. To change an image, you will need to edit the image property of the page.

Go to homepage carousel folder in AEM

Tip: Image order in the carousel matches the page order in AEM

items.title: Changing the image
items.text:
1. In the Homepage Banner folder, select the page for the carousel image you want to change.

items.title: YouTube video feeds
items.text:
There are many YouTube feeds on the CERG website. Some feeds automatically pull in videos from a YouTube playlist, while others are manually curated to show specific videos.

The feed is always inside a green HTML/embedded code component:

items.title: Feed properties
items.text:
Every feed is controlled by a small set of settings. You won't need all of them at once. Which ones you fill in depends on what you want the feed to show:

Setting What it does How to use it Videos data-videos Shows specific videos that you choose. Paste in one or more YouTube links separated by commas. Playlist data-playlist Automatically shows the newest videos from a YouTube playlist. However the playlist is sorted on YouTube, it shows the videos in that order. Paste in the playlist link. Only one is supported. Max videos data-max-videos How many videos to show. Only matters when you're using Playlist. With Videos, the feed just shows however many you listed. Enter in a number; default is 2. Title style data-title-style Controls how each video's title looks. Default is regular (bold text). Set to heading if the feed is more prominent on the page.

Videos > Playlist

If you fill in both Videos and Playlist, the feed will show the hand-picked videos you listed in Videos. The Playlist setting will be ignored.

Displays nothing if no videos or playlist are set

This is expected. It ensures the feed can be used safely in templates without configuration when no videos or playlists are needed.

items.title: How to set up a new feed
items.text:
1. Add an HTML component into a column control component wherever the feed should sit. Ensure it takes up less than 50% of the page width, otherwise the feed will look big.
  2. Click edit. It will open a coding text box in a new tab.

  3. Paste in the following code: 

    <script src="https://www.sfu.ca/content/dam/sfu/politics/CERG/code/js/iframe.js"></script>
 <iframe class="sfu-video-embed"
     src="https://cerg-youtube-feed.pages.dev/latest-videos-styled"

     data-videos=""
     data-playlist=""
     data-max-videos="2"
     data-title-style="regular"

     title="CERG Youtube Feed" width="100%" height="800px" frameborder="no"
     allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
     style="border-style: none; overflow: hidden; transition: height 0.2s ease;">
 </iframe>

  4. Fill in one of the settings — either data-videos or data-playlist, following the details for the feed properties for whichever you're using.

  5. Press the save button in the top left and close the coding window.
  6. To see the feed before publishing, switch to preview mode and reload the page. The feed should show up in the column you added it to.
  7. Activate the page.

items.title: How to change an existing feed
To show a YouTube playlist
items.text:
1. Copy the playlist link from YouTube. It should look like this: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLHSY2zpB60yE
  2. Click the Edit button on the HTML component.
  3. Make sure data-videos is empty. It should be left as an empty string: data-videos="".
  4. Paste the playlist link into the data-playlist setting.
  5. If you want to show a specific number of videos, change the data-max-videos setting.
  6. Press the save button in the top left and close the coding window.
  7. To see the feed before publishing, switch to preview mode and reload the page.
  8. Activate the page.

items.title: To show specific videos
items.text:
1. Find your video links from YouTube. They should look like this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video_id
  2. Click the Edit button on the HTML component.
  3. Make sure data-playlist is empty. It should be left as an empty string: data-playlist="".
  4. Paste the video links into the data-videos setting, separated by commas.
  5. If you want to show a specific number of videos, change the data-max-videos setting.
  6. Press the save button in the top left and close the coding window.
  7. To see the feed before publishing, switch to preview mode and reload the page.
  8. Activate the page.

items.title: To show the homepage
items.text:
1. Fill in data-playlist="" with the channel's uploads playlist ID: 

    UURAuV8XqQM0MD3VK_Pi32AA

  2. Make sure data-videos is empty. It should be left as an empty string: data-videos="".

  3. To see the feed before publishing, switch to preview mode and reload the page.
  4. Activate the page.

  3. Change the information in the new card by right clicking on it and selecting Edit. Make sure to update all necessary information.
  4. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Example of adding a second team member preview card on the Agrivoltaics page

items.title: Copy and Paste to different pages
items.text:
Unfortunately, there is no way to copy and paste components between different pages in AEM. If you want to copy a component from one page to another, you will need to manually create the component on the new page and manually copy over the design and content.

Things to copy: 1. Any text and image content. 1. CSS classes and styles for the component and its column control (if applicable). 1. Any other settings for the component (e.g. number of columns, pagination, captions, etc.).

Custom Components & Source Edit

If you're having troubles copying a specific design, select the source edit button (the far right button in the text editor) and copy the raw HTML code over to the new component. Paste it in the new component's source edit mode as well. This will ensure the design is copied over exactly.

Source edit button in the text editor

Source edit enabled in the text editor

items.title: Design
items.text: We follow SFU's Web Communicators Toolkit for the CERG website. The following is a summary of the most important design guidelines for the CERG website.

items.title: CERG Colours
items.text:
We follow SFU's brand colours for the CERG website.

However, we have a few additional colours that are used for the Working Paper topics. These colours are used in the Publications & Multimedia page , the Agrivoltaics hub , and in Working Paper Cover pages.

items.title: Update text content
items.text:
1. Right click on the text you want to edit and select Edit.
  2. Make your changes in the text editor that appears.
  3. Use the formatting buttons a the top of the editor to format your text, add links, or (rarely) add images.
  4. Press the OK button and Activate the page to save your changes.

Text with {{ }}

Don't edit text inside curly brackets {{ }} — it's a variable placeholder auto-filled by the site, and editing it breaks the component.

If that text needs to change (e.g., event, working paper, or news article info), update it via the documentation for that content type instead; changes will automatically reflect on your page.

Custom Components & Source Edit

If you're having troubles editing specific content, it might have custom inline styles applied. In order to ensure the design is kept intact, select the source edit button (the far right button in the text editor) and find the text to edit. Keep the styles the same.

Source edit button in the text editor

items.title: Activating a page, image, document
items.text: Every time you make a change to a page, image, or document in AEM, you need to activate it for the changes to be reflected on the CERG website.

items.title: While editing inside a page
items.text: When editing inside a page, you can click the Page icon in your tooibar, then select Activate Page.

items.title: Activate an image or document
items.text: When uploading or pasting images or documents, you can right click on the image or document and select Activate.

items.title: Updating an image
items.text:
Prerequisite

You have already uploaded the image to AEM that you want to use. If you haven't done this, follow the steps in Uploading new photos and documents.

If you're replacing an image, make sure to keep the same aspect ratio as the original or within the recommended aspect ratios given to you in instructions for that content. Otherwise, the design will worsen and may not look good on certain screen sizes.

To edit an image, right click on the image and select Edit. You can then drag and drop a new image into the Image field from the sidebar. Press the Crop button to crop the image to the recommended aspect ratio.

items.title: Upload the Working Paper PDF to AEM and Google Drive
items.text:
Prerequisites

You must be signed into your SFU account and have access to AEM in order to make changes. If you do not have access, please contact Andy to request access.

You also must have access to the CERG Google Drive folder in order to upload the PDF. If you do not have access, please contact Omri to request access.

You must have the PDF of the Working Paper ready to upload and the necessary content ready to fill in the page (title, overview, authors, etc.).

Upload the document to the Publications folder in AEM's DAM (Digital Asset Manager) and to the Working Papers folder in Google Drive:

Publications Folder in DAM Publications Folder in Google Drive

After uploading in Google Drive, copy the link to the PDF by right clicking on the file and selecting Share -> Copy link. We will need that link later to add the PDF Embed.

Updating the working paper

If you need to update the Working Paper PDF, AEM has a feature to overwrite the existing file. That way, you can simply upload the new PDF and not have to worry about changing anything:

Similar with Google Drive: upload the file with the exact same file name and it will overwrite the existing file. No need to change the link in the page.

items.title: Copy Working Paper template
items.text:
In AEM, navigate to the Publications & Multimedia page and copy the Working Paper template.

  1. Go to the Publications & Multimedia page
  2. Right click on the Working Paper Template (2026) and select Copy.]
  3. Click Paste to paste the template. Change the Copy name to this structure: wp-xx-short-title where xx is the number of the Working Paper and short-title is a 3-6 word keywords of the title (e.g., wp-21-fossil-fuel-alternatives-economy-diversification).
  4. The new page will show up at the end of the list of pages. You may have to go to the next page to see it.

items.title: Fill in Page Properties
items.text:
Here we add the following information into the Page Properties of the new Working Paper page:

Content to be added Type of content Where it goes Title The first portion of the Working Paper title, before the colon (if applicable) Basic -> Title Tags The keywords associated with the Working Paper Basic -> Tags/Keywords Date The date the Working Paper was published (both short 09/13/2026 and long formats September 13, 2026) Basic -> Date and Advanced -> Custom Properties -> custom-publication-date Subtitle (if applicable) The second portion of the Working Paper title, after the colon (if applicable) Basic -> More Titles and Description -> Subtitle Overview A brief layman's summary of the Working Paper's content (max. 70 words) Basic -> More Titles and Description -> Description Working Paper Number The number assigned to the Working Paper Advanced -> Custom Properties -> custom-publication-type Image (if applicable) The cover image of the Working Paper as a 3:2 (Carousel) aspect ratio Image
  1. Open up the page.
  2. Select Page Properties from the Page menu.
  3. Go through the three tabs in the Page Properties dialog and fill in the information above. If you don't have a cover image, you can leave the image field blank.

Filling in this information in Page Properties will automatically populate the Working Paper page with that information.

items.title: Adding Tags
items.text:
Tags are used to filter Working Papers by topic on the Publications & Multimedia page and Agrivoltaics page and to connect news items.

You must include the following tags for the Working Paper in the following order to appear in the correct places:

Type of tag Why Tag Name Topic To identify the topic of the Working Paper See a list of topics here. Publication Number The number assigned to the Working Paper X where X is the number of the Working Paper (e.g. 21) Publication Medium To identify it as a Working Paper; already on the template Working Paper working_paper

Topic tag must come first

Due to AEM restrictions, the topic tag must be the first tag in the list. If it is not, the Working Paper will not show the topic throughout the site.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

Video filling in Page Properties [coming soon]

items.title: Editing the Working Paper page
items.text:
While most content is added through Page Properties, some content is added directly to the page. This includes:

Content to be added Type of content Where it goes Authors The authors of the Working Paper Red box component Working Paper Download Button The link to download the Working Paper Red box component Press Release (if applicable) The link to download the Press Release Red box component PDF Embed The PDF Google Drive link Green HTML component below red box Videos (if applicable) Any videos related to the Working Paper Green HTML component beside red box News Setting up to automatically display news about the Working Paper List component that says "No Results Found"

The location of each piece of content that needs to be changed

items.title: Adding Authors and PDF Link
items.text:
1. Right click on the red box component and select Edit.
  2. Enter the names of the authors of the Working Paper, linking to their CERG profile or LinkedIn (if available).
  3. Change the link of the Press Release button to the Press Release PDF. Delete if there's no Press Release.
  4. Change the link of the Working Paper button to the Working Paper PDF.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Video showing how to add authors and PDF links

items.title: Adding PDF Embed
items.text:
1. Ensure you've uploaded the PDF to Google Drive and copied the link to it.
  2. Below the red box, click the green HTML component's Edit button.
  3. In the HTML editor, paste the Google Drive link to the PDF that you copied earlier into the quotation marks "" of the src attribute of the <iframe> tag.
  4. Change the ending of the link from /view?usp=drive_link to /preview. This will allow the PDF to be embedded in the page instead of opening in a new tab.
  5. Save the changes and close the HTML editor.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Video showing how to add PDF embed

items.title: Adding related YouTube video (i.e. webinar recordings)
items.text:
1. Beside the red box, click the green HTML component's Edit button.
  2. In the HTML editor, add any videos related to the Working Paper. If there are no videos, delete the entire <div> element that contains the "Featured In" section.

Follow the instructions in YouTube video feeds to add specific videos to the feed.

items.title: Configure related news list
items.text:
Please follow instructions carefully

Please do not alter any other setting or text in the List component. It might break.

  1. Right click on the List component beside the red box and select Edit.
  2. Go to the Advanced Search tab

  3. At the bottom of the text box, there should be a line that says:

    2_property.value=politics:cerg/publication/number/X

  4. Change the X to the number of the Working Paper (e.g. 21).

  5. Press the OK button. If you don't have any news items related to the Working Paper, it will say "No Results Found". If you do have news items, they will automatically show up in this section.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Video showing how to configure the news list

items.title: Activate
items.text:
You can preview the page by clicking the Preview button in your toolbar and reloading the page.

If everything looks good and the paper is ready for publication, Activate the page to save your changes and publish the paper.

items.title: Applying a Working Paper Template
items.text: There are cover templates for Working Papers that can be applied in Microsoft Word. There are 4 templates available for each of the 6 topics.

items.title: Choose a template
items.text:
1. Determine which topic your Working Paper is about. The topics are:

    • Agrivoltaics
    • Alternative Energy Sources
    • Community & Indigenous Energy
    • Energy Policy
    • True Cost of Fossil Fuels
    • Other Works

  2. Go to the Working Paper Templates folder in OneDrive:

    Working Paper Templates folder in OneDrive

  3. Select the folder of your topic

  4. Download which template variant matches your needs based on the number of authors and if you plan to include an image on the cover.

items.title: Apply the template to your Working Paper
items.text:
1. Open your Working Paper in Microsoft Word.
  2. Open the template you downloaded in Microsoft Word.
  3. Fill out the template with your Working Paper's information (title, authors, date, etc.). Replace the image if applicable.
  4. Copy your Working Paper content and paste it into the template below the header.

If there are formatting issues when pasting

If you're stuck trying to endlessly format your content after pasting, undo the pasting and try merging the two documents with an online tool like SmallPDF instead. This will preserve the formatting of your Working Paper while applying the template to the first page.

items.title: Export the Working Paper as a PDF
items.text: Export your Working Paper with the naming scheme wp-XX-title-of-paper.pdf where XX is the number of the Working Paper. For example, if your Working Paper is number 23 and titled "The Future of Solar Energy", the file name should be wp-23-the-future-of-solar-energy.pdf.

items.title: Add the Working Paper to the website
items.text: Once your Working Paper is ready, you can follow the instructions in Adding a Working Paper to add it to the website.

items.title: Creating a team member
items.text:
Prerequisites

You must be signed into your SFU account and have access to AEM in order to make changes. If you do not have access, please contact Andy to request access.

Have these details for the team member ready to fill in the page:

  • Name
  • What they do (i.e. Political Science professor @ SFU)
  • Bio (paragraph or two about their work/research)
  • Contact Information (i.e. LinkedIn profile, email)
  • Headshot photo (square, 1:1 ratio, at least 500px x 500px)
path: How to add a team member

items.text:
In AEM, navigate to the CERG Team page and copy the Team Member Template.

CERG Team page in AEM's WMC

  1. In the events page, right click on the Team Member Template and select Copy.
  2. Click Paste to paste the template. Change the Copy name to this structure: firstname-lastname where:
    • firstname is the team member's first name
    • lastname is the team member's last name (if applicable)
  3. The new page will show up at the end of the list of pages. You may have to go to the next page to see it.
